name: Exact Root-Gluing Width
statement: Let rooted classes $A_i\subseteq\{0,1\}^{F_i}$ contain zero on pairwise disjoint coordinate blocks and set $X=\bigcup_iA_i$. Then $\sigma(X;\{0\})=\max_i\sigma(A_i;\{0\})$ and $\sigma(X)=\min_k\max(\{\sigma(A_k)\}\cup\{\sigma(A_i;\{0\}):i\ne k\})$. In particular, two or more copies of one rooted class $A$ have width exactly $\sigma(A;\{0\})$.
proof: Apply bounded common-section composition with the singleton section $D=\{0\}$. The selected subset is empty or a singleton. The empty choice cannot improve on a singleton choice because $\sigma(A_k)\leq\sigma(A_k;\{0\})$, yielding both exact formulas.
comments: Root doubling realizes every prescribed-root width as an absolute width with at most twice as many concepts. Since root gluings preserve ample classes and partial cubes, absolute and prescribed-root widths have the same attainable ranges within each of those two families.
